title: Celebrity audiences and the show renamed The Hoofers
summary: At the Mercury Theater with celebrity audiences the show broke records and was renamed The Hoofers; Green mentions Derby Wilson.

So what, this is tape number 24, the last final tape of Mr. Chuck Green. So, Chuck, what basically happened to the show? What was really the cause of its decline, and why it eventually really didn't make it? When it moved to the Mercury Theater what happened?

Well, it really -- it became another sensation. It starts -- it broke its own record. You see, because people like Celeste Holms, Mrs. Hoot Gibson, Bert Wheeler, Bert Law's sister, you know, and Henny Youngman, Soupy Sales, see, Dorothy Townson and people like that was happening to be in these audiences.
And they came up on stage, see. At that time I was still -- the show had changed, see. I had -- me and Bojangles
Robinson's real protege in real life, Derbie Davie Wilson, you know -- he's the discoverer of Pearl Bailey's tap dancing brother, the minister's son, Bill Bailey.
Did the show change its name when it moved to the Mercury Theater?
And what happened when it moved to the Mercury Theater? Was it getting the same kind of publicity? The same kind of backing?
Well, it had better backing because it was beginning to get busloads, you know. The shut-ins was beginning to arrive, see, because they was -- they had demanded to see what this show was all about.
Well, how long did the show last in the Mercury Theater?
Oh, I'm telling you, it lasted from early '68 until late '69.
I thought that was at the other theater, the Bert Wheeler Theater.
